rv.q: Verdin's fast-paced and verbose production benefits from a sizzling little cast of Nick Sandys, Ryan Hallahan, Felipe Carrasco and, as the classy leading players, Elizabeth Laidlaw and Lucy Carapetyan.
It’s a satisfying thriller that breathes new life into a potentially musty script.
Already extended through the New Year, this is one exciting play theatergoers won’t want to miss!
You will be stunned by its simple beauty, its captivating acting, and its heart-pounding suspense.
Rooted in cat-and-mouse games and fraught with tension, it’s a tale skillfully told by a director who knows how to keep her audience engaged.
It's simply a murder story most deftly told. Which makes for an incredibly satisfying night out at the theater.
Suspenseful and fun with a stand-out team of artists, Dial M for Murder is a roller coaster from start to finish.

It all ticks along like a stylish and well-oiled clock, with Hallahan's villainous husband and Laidlaw's protective Maxine both focused on Carapetyan's frazzled and vulnerable Margot for completely different motives.
This is an excellent staging of an intriguing and suspenseful murder saga, and “Dial M for Murder” is certain to leave you satisfied.

For a few hours, the twists and turns of a good mystery well performed and well directed transport the audience into an easier world where people get what they deserve, and problems are satisfactorily solved.
This is two hours of fun and games with an ending that will make you feel good.
This clever adaption is well worth the watch.

cn.t: This stylish thriller revival earns praise for its progressive update and stellar performances, though the dialogue-heavy, static staging won't work for everyone. Critics highlight the suspenseful cat-and-mouse game and sharp direction.
